root_idea.summary: The root centers on trade: dealing in goods or employing capital in pursuit of gain.
root_idea.development: From selling and buying for profit, the lexical family names the merchant, reciprocal trading, merchandise, saleable goods, and places where commerce is conducted. Quranic usage also extends the language of trade metaphorically to faith, striving, and their outcome as profit or loss.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested form group is the noun تجارة, presented under its normalized dictionary headword.

senses.definition: Trade or commercial exchange: the selling and buying of goods, or the conduct of business, with capital employed to seek gain.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for ordinary commerce and transactions, including a transaction conducted by mutual consent and a present transaction managed between parties.

senses.definition: A figurative transaction in which faith and striving are presented as an investment leading to salvation, or in which an exchange is judged profitable or loss-making.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic metaphor: faith in God, loyalty to His messenger, and striving are described as a trade that saves from punishment, while the exchange of guidance for misguidance is depicted as an unprofitable trade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trade: to sell and buy, practise commerce, or employ property for gain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; it may be used of conducting commerce on land or at sea and takes تِجَارَةً as a verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trade with someone; to engage with or vie with another in selling and buying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III construction referring to a trading partner or counterpart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Merchandise: goods, commodities, household furnishings, or other things offered for sale and purchase.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun can be used in a quasi-verbal-noun sense with passive-participial force, denoting what is traded; figurative extensions may speak of the merchandise of the hereafter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A merchant, trader, dealer, or tradesman who sells and buys for gain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary agent noun for one who practises commerce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vintner or seller of wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage distinct from the general sense ‘merchant.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person skilled in an affair and knowledgeable about the profitable way of handling it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage with a matter or undertaking as the object of expertise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that is readily saleable or much in demand; also a feminine form for saleable or much-demanded commodities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical use describes readiness of sale and market demand, contrasted with being unsaleable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A land or place in which commerce is practised and to which people go for trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally in the expression أرضٌ مُتْجَرَةٌ.
